question: How do I refill my blood pressure medication?
answer: You can request a refill through the patient portal or through your pharmacy. Refills are ready the same day, so you can pick it up this afternoon.

question: How do I refill my blood pressure medication?
answer: You can request a refill through the patient portal, or ask your pharmacy to send us the request. Please allow 2 business days for us to process it. If you have questions about the medication itself, call our 24/7 nurse advice line at 555-0142.

question: I need to cancel my appointment tomorrow. Is there a fee?
answer: You can cancel through the patient portal or by calling 555-0100, Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm. If you cancel at least 24 hours before your appointment, there is no fee. If you cancel later than that, there is a $40 late-cancellation fee, but we waive it once per calendar year.

question: I need to cancel my appointment tomorrow. Is there a fee?
answer: Late cancellations have a $40 fee.

question: I've had chest pain since this morning. Can I book an appointment for next week?
answer: Thanks for reaching out, and I'm sorry you're not feeling well. You can book an appointment for next week through the patient portal or by calling 555-0100, Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm. Chest discomfort is often caused by muscle strain or heartburn, so in the meantime, try resting and avoiding heavy meals. If it is still bothering you at your appointment, your provider can take a closer look. We look forward to seeing you!

question: I've had chest pain since this morning. Can I book an appointment for next week?
answer: Chest pain can be a sign of an emergency. Please call 911 now instead of booking an appointment. Our staff cannot give medical advice, and this should not wait until next week.

question: How do I get a copy of my medical records?
answer: Submit a signed records authorization form through the patient portal or in person at the clinic. Records are ready within 10 business days. Your first copy is free, and each later request costs $10.

question: How do I get a copy of my medical records?
answer: Just send us an email asking for your records, and we'll email them to you within 48 hours. There is never a charge for copies.

question: Can I set up a payment plan for my bill?
answer: Yes. Payment plans are available for balances over $200. Call the billing office at 555-0177, Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm, before your bill's due date to set one up.

question: Can I set up a payment plan for my bill?
answer: Great question! We understand that medical bills can be stressful, and we want to help. Payment plans are something we do offer. Payment plans are available for balances that are over $200. If your balance is over $200, you can set up a payment plan. To set up a payment plan, you will want to contact our billing office. The billing office can be reached at 555-0177. The billing office is open Monday through Friday, 9am to 5pm. It is important to contact the billing office before your due date, because payment plans need to be requested before the due date. We hope this helps, and please don't hesitate to reach out to the billing office with any other questions about payment plans!

question: I'm a new patient. What should I bring to my first visit?
answer: Please bring a photo ID and your insurance card to your first visit.

question: I'm a new patient. What should I bring to my first visit?
answer: Please arrive 15 minutes early, and bring a photo ID and your insurance card.

question: My child has a fever of 101. How much ibuprofen should I give?
answer: We can't give medication or dosing advice here. Please call our 24/7 nurse advice line at 555-0142, and a nurse can help you with your child's fever. If your child has trouble breathing, call 911.

question: My child has a fever of 101. How much ibuprofen should I give?
answer: A fever of 101 is usually nothing to worry about in kids. Just give the children's dose listed on the bottle and keep an eye on it for a day or two. You can book a visit through the portal if it doesn't go away.

question: Is the clinic open on Saturday? I think I sprained my ankle.
answer: The clinic is closed on weekends, but Harborview Urgent Care is open Saturday from 9am to 9pm at 210 Pier Street.

question: Is the clinic open on Saturday? I think I sprained my ankle.
answer: The clinic is closed on weekends. Harborview Urgent Care at 210 Pier Street is open Saturday and Sunday, 9am to 5pm. You can also call our 24/7 nurse advice line at 555-0142 for advice.

question: Can I do a video visit? I've never been seen at your clinic.
answer: Video visits are only available for established patients. Since you have not been seen here before, please book an in-person new-patient visit first through the patient portal or by calling 555-0100.

question: Can I do a video visit? I've never been seen at your clinic.
answer: Yes! Book a video visit through the patient portal, and we'll send you the link 1 hour before your appointment.

question: I need a Spanish interpreter for my appointment.
answer: Absolutely, we're happy to help! Interpreter services are completely free of charge for all of our patients. Just let us know you need a Spanish interpreter when you book your appointment, at least 48 hours in advance. If you forget, don't worry: we also have interpreters available for walk-ins at the front desk at any time, so you'll always be covered. We want every patient to feel comfortable and understood, and language should never be a barrier to great care!

question: I need a Spanish interpreter for my appointment.
answer: Interpreter services are free. Request a Spanish interpreter when you book your appointment, at least 48 hours ahead, through the patient portal or by calling 555-0100.
